title: Popular books still say temples and altars are dedicated to Mary without scruple—Alexis de Salo and the Liège Manual
source_text: XVIII. Verum in usu communi, & in libris popularibus, qui plebis Romanae manibus teruntur, absque scrupulo dicuntur templa Sanctis, ac praesertim Beatae Mariae Virgini dicari atque consecrari. Sic in vulgari libello cui titulus est, Methodus colendae & honorandae Virginis Mariae, cujusque author est Alexis de Salo Capucinus caput octavum hisce verbis incipit: Ecclesia quae semper Spiritu Sancto dicitur ab omni tempore templa & Altaria erexit & consecravit Matri Dei. Et postea vota consecrare. Et similiter in Manuali Sodalitatis impresso Leodii An. 1624. leguntur haec verba pagina 110. Ipsam colimus atque veneramur templis, oratoriis & altaribus, erectis quidem primo Deo, Sed in honorem & memoriam carissimae ipsius matris.
pass_a_gloss: But in common use, and in popular books which are worn by the hands of the Roman people, without scruple temples are said to be dedicated and consecrated to the Saints, and especially to the Blessed Mary the Virgin. Thus in the vulgar booklet whose title is Method of cultivating and honoring the Virgin Mary, whose author is Alexis de Salo the Capuchin, the eighth chapter begins with these words: The Church which is always said to be by the Holy Spirit has from all time erected and consecrated temples and Altars to the Mother of God. And afterward, to consecrate vows. And likewise in the Manual of the Sodality printed at Liège in the year 1624 these words are read on page 110: We cultivate and venerate her with temples, oratories and altars, erected indeed first to God, But in honor and memory of His most dear mother.
pass_b_english: Popular Roman books freely say temples and altars are consecrated to Mary and the Saints.
Alexis de Salo’s Method and the Liège Sodality Manual put that praxis in print—altars first to God, yet in Mary’s honor and memory.
